sub_graphs.title: EIP-8025: Execution Proof Request Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the lifecycle of proof generation requests from initiation to delivery

nodes.label: New Payload Request Received
nodes.description: A NewPayloadRequest has been received by the consensus layer requiring proof-based validation

nodes.label: Request Proof Generation
nodes.description: Call request_proofs(request, proof_attributes) to initiate asynchronous proof generation, returns ProofGenId

nodes.label: Proof Generation In Progress
nodes.description: Proof generation is underway, tracked by ProofGenId; system awaits async delivery

nodes.label: Execution Proof Delivered
nodes.description: Generated proof delivered via beacon API endpoint POST /eth/v1/prover/execution_proofs

nodes.label: Verify Execution Proof
nodes.description: Call verify_execution_proof(proof) to validate the delivered execution proof; returns boolean

nodes.label: Execution Proof Valid
nodes.description: Proof verified successfully; execution payload can be accepted without full state

nodes.label: Execution Proof Invalid
nodes.description: Proof verification failed; payload must be rejected

edges.label: Proof generation started; ProofGenId returned for tracking
Proof delivered asynchronously via beacon API

sub_graphs.title: EIP-8025: Payload Request Header Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation of new payload request headers against stored proof state

nodes.label: New Payload Request Header Received
nodes.description: A new payload request header needs validation against existing proof state

nodes.label: Verify Payload Header Against Proof State
nodes.description: Call verify_new_payload_request_header() to check stored proofs match the request header

nodes.label: Payload Header Valid
nodes.description: Header validation passed; corresponding execution is valid per stored proofs

nodes.label: Payload Header Invalid
nodes.description: Header does not match stored proof state; request rejected

sub_graphs.title: EIP-8025: Proof Delivery Trust Boundary
sub_graphs.description: Models the trust boundaries around asynchronous proof delivery via the beacon API

nodes.label: Awaiting Proof Delivery
nodes.description: System waiting for async proof delivery; vulnerable to delayed or missing proofs

nodes.label: Receive Proof via Beacon API
nodes.description: Accept execution proof delivered via POST /eth/v1/prover/execution_proofs endpoint

nodes.label: Validate Proof Format and Type
nodes.description: Check that delivered proof matches requested proof_types from ProofAttributes

nodes.label: Proof Stored in ProofState
nodes.description: Validated proof stored in proof_state for later use in header verification

edges.label: Proof delivered to beacon API endpoint
Proof accepted and stored in proof_state
External prover delivers proof via API

external_entities.name: External Prover
external_entities.description: Implementation-dependent proof generator delivering proofs asynchronously via beacon API

ambiguities.text: Validation functions are 'implementation dependent' with no specified behavior
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume each implementation must provide cryptographic proof verification that ensures execution validity. The interface contract (boolean return) is the only guaranteed behavior.

ambiguities.text: No specification of what happens if proof delivery times out or is never received
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the system must handle timeout cases; likely falls back to full execution validation or rejects the payload.

ambiguities.text: ProofType is referenced but not enumerated; unclear what proof types exist
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume ProofType is an extensible enum defined elsewhere; the proof engine must support all types listed in ProofAttributes.

implicit_assumptions.description: The external proof engine is trusted to generate correct proofs; the consensus layer only verifies, it does not generate proofs itself
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A compromised proof engine could generate false proofs, allowing invalid execution payloads to be accepted

implicit_assumptions.description: The beacon API endpoint POST /eth/v1/prover/execution_proofs is only accessible to authorized proof engines
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An attacker could submit forged proofs via the API endpoint, bypassing execution validation

implicit_assumptions.description: Proof generation completes within a reasonable time bound relative to slot duration
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Delayed proof delivery could cause missed slots or force fallback to full execution
